negative_findings.description: No public ČNB register of individually approved persons (a searchable 'seznam osob se souhlasem s výkonem funkce' listing approved board members and key function holders) was found in either cs or en searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: ČNB publishes entity registers (JERRS) and final enforcement decisions, but approvals of individual statutory-body members appear not to be published as a person-level list; the observable trace is the downstream commercial-register entry.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's highest-precision hypothesis — a machine-readable feed of approved individuals — does not hold as stated. A5 leadership detection for CZ must be built on ČNB entity registers joined to obchodní rejstřík officer diffs, not on a ČNB person register.

negative_findings.description: The 30-day advance notification duty for changes in the composition of statutory bodies and supervisory boards (reported in secondary legal press, tied to §8ab of the Banking Act) has no located public disclosure channel.
negative_findings.result_summary: Notifications are filed to ČNB; no public feed, gazette section or dataset publishing these prior notifications was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The earliest possible leadership signal (~30 days pre-change) exists in law but is not observable, which caps how early A5 can detect CZ bank board moves through official channels.

negative_findings.description: Exact deep-link forms for the JERRS application, the ČNB press-release cs listing, the annual supervision report landing page, and the ARES canonical domain were not confirmed by fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search surfaced variant URLs (apl.cnb.cz login/error path, /export/sites PDF paths, ares.cz vs ares.gov.cz, mf.gov.cz vs mfcr.gov.cz); the parent pages that were fetched (seznamy hub, open data) resolved cleanly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must resolve these variants before collectors are pinned; a 404 on a guessed deep link should not be read as the source being dead.

negative_findings.description: Access terms, rate limits and any registration requirement for WS JERRS were not established.
negative_findings.result_summary: The documentation page describes three XML services and a standardised request/response flow, but the fetch summary did not expose endpoint URLs, WSDL location, or usage conditions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: WS JERRS is the cell's best automation target; unresolved access terms are the main implementation risk for the whole A5 CZ register pipeline.

negative_findings.description: Air Bank has a 'Pro novináře' page but no year-partitioned press-release archive comparable to KB/ČS/rb.cz was surfaced; the site's contact route for media/marketing is a generic address (marketing@airbank.cz).
negative_findings.result_summary: Only /pro-novinare/ and annual-report PDFs confirmed as durable Air Bank primary surfaces.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Air Bank leadership moves may need to be caught via PPF group communications or secondary media rather than a bank newsroom feed.

negative_findings.description: For UniCredit Bank CZ, Banka CREDITAS and Partners Banka I did not surface the canonical Czech press-centre index URL in search results — only an /en/ subpage (UniCredit), the site root (Creditas), or a single article slug (Partners Banka).
negative_findings.result_summary: Newsroom existence is near-certain for all three but the exact listing paths were not observed and are recorded as best-guess entry points with lowered confidence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A crawler seeded on a guessed index path would silently collect nothing; these three need a nav-resolution pass before scheduling.

negative_findings.description: Czech-domiciled payment institutions (Global Payments Česko, Worldline CZ) show no dense Czech-language press-release stream on their own domains; searches on 'platební instituce' + 'tisková zpráva' + appointment terms returned company/contact pages rather than appointment announcements.
negative_findings.result_summary: No CZ payment-institution appointment press release found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The A5 signal for non-bank PSPs will have to come from wires (Protext), registry filings, or LinkedIn-type surfaces rather than corporate newsrooms — a structural gap in this cell, not a search failure.

negative_findings.description: Raiffeisenbank's 2026 press-release folders surfaced only product news (business services, mobile banking); the only board-change release observed on rb.cz dates to 2018.
negative_findings.result_summary: No 2026 Raiffeisenbank leadership announcement located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence of a hit in search is not absence of a release; the year/month folder enumeration should be run directly rather than relying on search indexing.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated public page was found linking Poštovní spořitelna / ČSOB's postal-counter banking arrangement to a specific state tender or to named programme owners on the state side.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches combining ČSSZ, Česká pošta and Poštovní spořitelna with 'státní zakázka' returned only generic civil-service vacancy and Czech Post recruitment pages; the ČSOB partnership is described only in marketing terms on ceskaposta.cz.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The postal-banking interface is a structurally important CZ public-sector payments channel; without a documented source, org changes there will only be visible indirectly via Czech Post vacancies and ČSOB press releases.

negative_findings.description: The Věstník veřejných zakázek appears to have migrated from vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz to vvz.nipez.cz, but this was not confirmed by fetching either host.

negative_findings.description: No confirmed machine-readable export or API was identified for ISoSS (portal.isoss.cz) civil-service vacancy data.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only descriptive references to ISoSS publication duties were found; the portal itself was not fetched and no dataset endpoint surfaced in search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ISoSS is the highest-value A5 feed in this cell; if only HTML scraping is possible, collection cost and fragility rise materially.

negative_findings.description: No municipal-level (Praha, Brno, Ostrava, kraje) buyer profile was identified for banking/payment services within this run.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Municipalities are a large, distinct segment of public-sector payment buying (fee collection, parking, card acceptance) with their own org units; leaving them out biases the cell toward central government.

negative_findings.description: NKÚ (Nejvyšší kontrolní úřad) audit reports were not searched in this run despite being an obvious 'who audits' category for state payments programmes.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: NKÚ audit conclusions routinely name programme owners, describe unit responsibilities and criticise governance — dense org-change evidence unavailable elsewhere.

negative_findings.description: Accenture does not appear to publish a Czech-language newsroom announcing CZ financial-services practice leadership. Searches in cs returned only generic CZ company profiles and country-lead appointments for other markets (Switzerland, Italy).

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated source entry and flags that the cell brief's event list needs correcting so downstream collection is not scheduled against a non-existent event.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Title-drift detection needs two editions. If no on-site archive exists, the collector must snapshot every crawl itself and backfill from the Wayback Machine, otherwise the first year yields no signal at all.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Signals to the run owner that hiring-volume topics must be carried by other cells (job boards, ATS pages, LinkedIn) — this cell should be scored on leadership-move and org-change detection only.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for a public, itemised register of hromadné propouštění notifications naming the employer. Úřad práce ČR publishes counts and sector breakdowns (press releases, regional annual reports, open data), but I found no evidence of a public per-employer notification register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Aggregate-only disclosure found; per-employer notifications appear not to be published, only aggregated (e.g. '15 notifications, up to 831 employees' in a month, with sector groupings like energy, clothing, machinery).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means firm-level detection of a Czech bank's collective redundancy must come from unions, media or ad-hoc ÚP/regional statements — the statutory notification itself is not a directly harvestable source. Consider an Info Act (zákon č. 106/1999 Sb.) request as a collection method.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for works councils (rada zaměstnanců) and European Works Councils (evropská rada zaměstnanců) specifically in Czech banks. Only generic legal/explanatory material was found (Labour Code Part 12, ČMKOS guide PDF, MPSV handbook, academic theses).
negative_findings.result_summary: No public register or directory of which Czech banks have a rada zaměstnanců or which are covered by an EWC of their foreign parent (Erste, KBC, Société Générale, UniCredit, Raiffeisen).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: EWC-level consultation is where group-wide offshoring/restructuring affecting the Czech subsidiary is first disclosed. Absent a register, coverage must be inferred from parent-group union federations (UNI Europa Finance) and from parent annual/sustainability reports.

negative_findings.description: OSPPP publishes the existence of a higher-level collective agreement (Kolektivní smlouva vyššího stupně, KSVS 2022-2025) in its documents section, but firm-level collective agreements at individual banks were not found publicly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the sector-level KSVS is publicly referenced; per-bank kolektivní smlouvy are not published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Firm-level agreements contain redundancy severance multiples and job-security clauses — high-value org-change intelligence that is only obtainable via the union or leaked/reported summaries. Also: the KSVS end-date 2022-2025 suggests a successor agreement should exist and be tracked.

negative_findings.description: Úřad práce ČR moved its web presence to up.gov.cz in February 2026; historical links live under uradprace.cz and mpsv.cz/up-cz.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three coexisting host patterns observed in search results for the same statistical pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector built on old paths will produce false 'dead source' verdicts. All ÚP URLs in this slice should be treated as unverified until a deterministic liveness pass resolves the current canonical host.

negative_findings.description: Direct cs-language search for Czech discussion-forum threads about bank reorganisations/layoffs returned no forum threads at all — only Wikipedia history pages and statistics.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The forum layer of this cell is currently unmapped; if a dedicated CZ finance-employee forum exists it would be the earliest signal source and is being missed.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: English-language Brno coverage aimed at the SSC expat workforce is a distinct sub-layer; leaving it unresolved is a real gap rather than an absence of the source.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The English-language employee-voice layer may be less accessible than Atmoskop, changing the collection plan for international SSC staff sentiment.

negative_findings.result_summary: Finextra/The Paypers confirmed as live appointment-covering outlets, but no evidence of systematic CZ people coverage. They should be treated as thin, opportunistic feeds rather than reliable CZ trackers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-weighting these two seed outlets in the collection plan; parent-company newsrooms carry the actual CZ signal.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief lists SeeNews as a seed; downgrading it avoids wasted crawl budget.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design should route wire coverage through licensed feeds or mirrors rather than assuming a scrapable desk page.

negative_findings.description: Robert Walters was named in the cell brief, but cs and en searches returned only Robert Walters Germany, Switzerland and Africa banking/financial-services pages plus unrelated CZ business-register entries for a person named 'Robert Walter'. No evidence surfaced of a Robert Walters Czech Republic office or CZ salary survey.
negative_findings.result_summary: No CZ-specific Robert Walters entity or publication found in this pass; the CZ market appears to be covered by Hays, Grafton, Reed, Randstad, Manpower and the retained-search boutiques instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents allocating collection effort to a source that may not exist for CZ; if Robert Walters covers CZ it is likely served remotely from Germany/Austria, so the DE site would be the place to look.

negative_findings.description: Talentica s.r.o. (talentica.cz), named in the cell brief, self-describes as a specialist agency for technically oriented professionals in automotive, mechanical/electrical engineering, electronics and IT, based in Prague 6 and Brno.
negative_findings.result_summary: Talentica is not a financial-services recruiter; no banking/payments salary or hiring publications found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Should be dropped from the CZ banking HR watchlist to avoid noise, unless tracked narrowly for bank IT/engineering hiring spillover.

negative_findings.description: Grafton Recruitment's full salary survey is explicitly distributed only to current or prospective client HR departments in electronic form; Hays' full guide and several Randstad/Reed reports appear to sit behind registration forms.
negative_findings.result_summary: The richest per-position banking pay data from recruiters is gated; only summary pages and press releases are openly collectable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must rely on PR republication (kurzy.cz, e15.cz, penize.cz, hrnews.cz) as the open proxy layer, or on a legitimate client relationship for the full datasets.

negative_findings.description: No CZ recruiter or headhunter was found publishing a dedicated banking/payments-only hiring or salary report; banking appears as one sector inside general multi-sector guides (Hays 12 specialisations, Grafton 9 sectors, Manpower MEOS 'finance, pojišťovnictví a nemovitosti').
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector granularity must be reconstructed from sector chapters and index values rather than from a dedicated banking talent report.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for extraction: the unit of collection is a sector chapter or a single index number, not a standalone banking report.

negative_findings.description: Personalista.com resolves over plain HTTP and search snippets showed mangled diacritics, suggesting a legacy/possibly semi-abandoned site. No fetch was performed to confirm.
negative_findings.result_summary: Listed as a candidate with low priority and an encoding caveat; liveness and update cadence unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should confirm whether the site still publishes before any crawler is pointed at it.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for the exact seed pattern 'vedoucí oddělení platebního styku' on Jobs.cz; no such live listing surfaced in results, only the category page and bank career portals.
negative_findings.result_summary: Category and employer portals found; no specific payments-department-head ad observed at search time.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell must be worked as a monitored time series (repeated diffs), not as a one-shot search — the signal is the appearance of such a role, which is rare and episodic.

negative_findings.description: Techloop, Cocuma and Jenda.cz — Czech tech-specific boards named in the search — did not surface in results; their current status (live, merged, or defunct) is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned only international boards (Glassdoor, Wellfound, EuroTechJobs, WeAreDevelopers) instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One or more CZ-native tech boards may be dead or rebranded; assuming they exist would risk a fabricated source. They need direct verification before being added.

negative_findings.description: No public RSS/API/open-data feed for CZ bank vacancies was identified on Jobs.cz, Prace.cz or StartupJobs.cz during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: All discovered access is HTML search UI; the ÚP/MPSV register is the only candidate for a structured official feed and its canonical endpoint was not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume HTML snapshotting under ToS constraints, or pursue the MPSV register as the compliant structured alternative.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn Jobs and Glassdoor — the two richest sources for senior/leadership CZ banking roles — both gate depth behind login and prohibit automated collection.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as blocked=true with manual-review-only collection methods.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The leadership-moves half of this cell cannot be automated; it needs analyst time budgeted, or a licensed data provider.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn post-level search is not reachable from a logged-out client. Public web search surfaces LinkedIn PROFILE pages (and their headline/summary text) but almost never individual 'nastupuji do' / 'excited to join' POST permalinks for CZ banking.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four idiom-based queries in cs and en returned profile URLs and unrelated pages, no retrievable post permalinks.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core premise — that individuals announce moves before their employer does — is true, but the announcement text itself is not machine-collectable at scale without LinkedIn credentials or a licensed data provider. Collection design must lean on profile-headline diffing plus press-side mirrors.

negative_findings.description: No Czech banking or payments professional/institutional accounts were identified on Bluesky beyond a generic #Czech hashtag feed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query for CZ banking/fintech on bsky.app returned bank websites and one hashtag page, no sector accounts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bluesky is the only openly crawlable microblog of the three; if the CZ banking community is not there, the open-data path for this cell is effectively closed and budget should go to LinkedIn-mirroring press instead.

negative_findings.description: Official X accounts were confirmed for Air Bank and Raiffeisenbank ČR, but no X account was confirmed for Komerční banka or ČSOB in this pass (Komerční banka appeared only via Facebook, Raiffeisenbank ČR also via Instagram).
negative_findings.result_summary: cs-language query for official CZ bank X profiles returned two X handles plus Facebook/Instagram alternates.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence here is unverified, not established — it should be retested before concluding the two largest banks have abandoned X, since X's own search is login-walled and search engines index it poorly.

negative_findings.description: No established Czech-language equivalent was found for 'alumni note' / 'leaver post' as a discrete content genre; Czech leavers write free-form 'po X letech odcházím' style posts with no canonical phrase, and no Czech bank alumni network page was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches produced no CZ bank alumni association or leaver-note convention.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Departures are the higher-signal half of org change (they precede a vacancy and often a strategy shift) and this run currently has no reliable local-language query handle for them.

negative_findings.description: The public part of the Evidence skutečných majitelů (esm.justice.cz) and its open data were made inaccessible by the Ministry of Justice on 17 December 2025.
negative_findings.result_summary: MSp announcement and FAU summary confirm public access and open data withdrawal; remaining access is via datová schránka for one's own extract, JIP for public authorities, or formal request.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Beneficial-ownership tracing of CZ payment institutions and fintech SPVs can no longer be done openly. Any A5 workflow that assumed ESM as a free ownership layer must be redesigned around commercial-register ownership data and pre-2026 archived ESM snapshots.

negative_findings.description: The amended Czech law on přeměny (transformations) removed the requirement to publish merger notices in Obchodní věstník; merger projects and creditor warnings are now deposited into the Sbírka listin at least one month before approval.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed across multiple CZ legal commentaries (epravo.cz, matidal.cz) surfaced by the Obchodní věstník query.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Monitoring Obchodní věstník alone will now MISS bank/fintech restructurings. The Sbírka listin document feed must be the primary M&A/restructuring early-warning channel for CZ.

negative_findings.description: Two register domains appear to be migrating: Obchodní věstník results now resolve under ov.gov.cz (seed assumed ov.justice.cz), and a new public-register portal verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz is running alongside or.justice.cz.
negative_findings.result_summary: Live search results returned ov.gov.cz record URLs and verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz search pages; the legacy ov.ihned.cz mirror also still appears.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any hardcoded collector URLs against ov.justice.cz or or.justice.cz carry migration risk; a URL-stability check should be part of the recurring pipeline rather than a one-off.

negative_findings.description: No statutory register source was found that records non-statutory HIRING — i.e. ordinary staff appointments, headcount, or department reorganisations below the statutory-body/prokura level.
negative_findings.result_summary: CZ registers cover only legally registered particulars: statutory body members, prokuristé, branch heads, ownership, registered office. Rank-and-file hiring simply is not a registrable fact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'jobs' and 'hiring' topics of this run cannot be served from this cell. They must come from job boards, LinkedIn, and press cells; this cell should be scoped to leadership moves and organisation/legal-entity changes only.

negative_findings.description: Merk.cz was named in the cell scope but was not independently confirmed by fetch in this pass; its access model, API availability and pricing are assumed, not observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Aggregator search surfaced Kurzy.cz, Peníze.cz, Finmag.cz and sledovani-insolvence.cz but did not return a Merk.cz result page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Its candidate record carries a deliberately reduced confidence_score; the verification pass should treat it as a priority liveness/capability check before any procurement decision.

negative_findings.description: The cell scope names 'ÚVIS' as a register source; no CZ register of that name relevant to corporate filings was found. ÚVIS (Úřad pro veřejné informační systémy) was abolished in the 2000s and its functions absorbed into the Ministry of Informatics/Interior.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches within this cell surfaced ISIR (insolvency) but nothing matching an active 'ÚVIS' filing register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The scope term is likely a stale artefact or a conflation with ISIR; the run definition should be corrected so a downstream collector does not chase a non-existent portal.

negative_findings.description: Searches in Czech and English did not surface a dedicated, separately addressable 'issuer announcements / oznámení emitentů' index page on pse.cz distinct from the general /zpravy (/en/news) feed. Fetching the MONETA ISIN detail page showed Overview, Tick Data, Historical Data, Company Profile, News and a corporate-calendar reference, but no announcements sub-page.
negative_findings.result_summary: PSE appears to route issuer regulated disclosures to the general news feed and out to issuer IR sites / ČNB CUri rather than hosting a MAR filing archive of its own. Unverified — the site is JS-heavy and a deeper crawl may reveal one.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector should treat ČNB CUri as the authoritative filing archive and pse.cz only as a timing tripwire; assuming PSE holds the filings would create silent gaps.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB CUri/OAM search application URL (oam.cnb.cz SIPRESWEB entry point) was obtained from search-result text and the ČNB landing page rather than by a direct successful fetch of the application itself.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with confidence 0.8; liveness and the exact query-parameter contract must be established by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most important source in the cell; if its endpoint has moved, the whole primary-filing channel silently fails.

negative_findings.description: No RSS/Atom or public API was identified for any of the Czech-side sources in this cell (pse.cz, investors.moneta.cz, kb.cz, csob.cz, ČNB CUri) during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: All Czech-side collection is likely to require HTML scraping plus PDF text extraction.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Drives collector design and cost; also raises brittleness risk versus the Austrian/Belgian parents where EQS and Euronext offer stable permalinks.

negative_findings.description: Česká spořitelna, ČSOB and Raiffeisenbank a.s. have no Czech equity listing, so no CZ-level MAR management-change disclosure exists for them; only bond-issuer disclosures and parent-level (Erste/KBC/RBI) ad-hoc releases cover their leadership.
negative_findings.result_summary: For three of the four largest CZ banks, this cell can only deliver A5 signal via foreign-parent disclosure plus annual-report governance chapters.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets a structural ceiling on this cell's coverage; CZ-entity board changes for these banks must be picked up by other cells (commercial register, ČNB licensing lists, press).

negative_findings.description: No standalone Czech 'payments association' equivalent to a national payments council was found. The functional equivalent is Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) plus ČBA's internal payments committees; SBK's web presence appears split across two domains and possibly stale.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched cs terms for a Czech payments association; only SBK and ČBA committee structures surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A scout expecting a single payments-association member directory will not find one; payments actor coverage must be assembled from SBK + ČBA committees + Czech Fintech Association.

negative_findings.description: Fetch of https://www.cbaonline.cz/o-nas/komise-pracovni-skupiny returned only navigation chrome with no committee or chair content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Page reachable but substantive content not extracted — likely client-side rendered or behind a content loader.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single richest people-source in this cell could not be read by a plain fetch; the collector will need a headless browser rather than static HTTP.

negative_findings.description: No German- or Czech-language finance/banking working group ('Arbeitskreis Finanzen', 'pracovní skupina finance') could be confirmed for ČNOPK (Deutsch-Tschechische Industrie- und Handelskammer), and no financial-services committee page was confirmed for the British Chamber of Commerce CZ.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in de/en returned only general chamber descriptions; no committee rosters located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two named chambers in the cell brief remain uncovered, so bilateral-chamber people-intelligence is incomplete.

negative_findings.description: AKAT's executive-director name appears inconsistently across sources (Jana Michalíková vs. Jana Brodani), and ČBA membership counts range 34-37 depending on source date.
negative_findings.result_summary: Secondary sources disagree; primary association pages were not fetched to resolve.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Person-level facts from aggregators must be re-anchored to the association's own site or the spolkový rejstřík before entering an intelligence record.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn association pages are the richest people-graph layer but are login-walled and their ToS prohibit scraping.
negative_findings.result_summary: Identified but marked collection_allowed=false.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated pipelines must not depend on LinkedIn; equivalent signal has to come from association sites, registry filings and trade press.

coverage_gaps.description: No person-level official feed links a named individual to an approved role at a named regulated CZ entity; the join must be reconstructed from entity registers plus commercial-register officer changes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Design the CZ A5 leadership collector as an IČO-keyed join: ČNB open data / WS JERRS for the regulated population → ARES/obchodní rejstřík statutory-body diffs → optional confirmation from company press releases.

coverage_gaps.description: ČNB open data covers only seven datasets (banks, exchange offices, consumer-credit providers and intermediaries) — payment institutions, e-money institutions and small-scale providers appear only via JERRS/WS JERRS, not as plain CSV.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm which JERRS roles WS JERRS exposes for PI/EMI/PSPMR and build the SOAP client; fall back to structured scraping of the JERRS UI only if the services do not cover those roles.

coverage_gaps.description: Sector self-regulatory and professional bodies adjacent to the statutory regulators (Česká bankovní asociace, Česká asociace pro platební styk / fintech associations) were not scouted in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a sibling cell to industry associations — they publish board and committee appointments naming senior bank and payments executives, complementing the regulator-side view.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language ČNB mirrors were confirmed for press releases and payments licensing, but it was not established whether the registers, open data and final-decision listings have equivalent en versions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: During verification, probe /en/ counterparts of each cs register URL and record whether the en mirror is complete or partial, so bilingual matching rules can be set.

coverage_gaps.description: No historical/archived snapshots of the CZ registers were identified, so back-testing leadership-change detection over past years is not currently possible from official sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Start own snapshot archiving immediately, and check whether the national open data catalogue (data.gov.cz) or web archives hold prior ČNB register versions.

coverage_gaps.description: Cell list omits several relevant CZ deposit-takers and specialised banks whose leadership moves matter to the same market map: Hypoteční banka, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida (KB group), Stavební spořitelna České spořitelny, Max banka, mBank CZ branch, ING CZ, J&T Banka, PPF banka, Wüstenrot.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the newsroom roster to these entities in a follow-up slice; group subsidiaries often announce director-level changes their parent bank does not.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell is newsroom-only by design, so it cannot see leadership changes that are legally registered but never announced (obchodní rejstřík / justice.cz filings of statutory-body changes, ČNB's list of licensed persons and management approvals).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair this cell with a registry/regulator cell (justice.cz, ČNB seznamy a evidence) so silent changes are still captured with exact legal effective dates.

coverage_gaps.description: Newsrooms cover appointments well but rarely cover ordinary hiring volume, team build-outs, or layoffs. The 'jobs/hiring' topic is therefore under-served by this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a careers-portal cell (kariera/kariéra subdomains of the same banks) plus job-board and works-council surfaces to carry the hiring-volume signal.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language mirrors exist for several issuers (fio.cz/about-us/media/press-releases, unicreditbank.cz/en/, csob.cz EN portal) but were not systematically enumerated; EN mirrors sometimes lag or omit local appointment releases.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Record cs/en URL pairs per issuer and always treat the cs page as authoritative for effective dates and titles.

coverage_gaps.description: No liveness or robots/ToS check was performed on any listed URL in this pass, and some portal URLs (ČSOB Liferay asset_publisher links) are query-parameter heavy and may not be stable canonical addresses.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic verification pass, and prefer canonical slugs over asset_publisher query URLs when seeding crawlers.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal and regional (obce, kraje, městské části) buyers of payment/acquiring services are unrepresented.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated cs pass on 'akceptace platebních karet obec', 'platební terminály město veřejná zakázka', 'kraj bankovní služby zakázka' across VVZ, NEN, Tender Arena, E-ZAK and Josephine buyer profiles.

coverage_gaps.description: Audit and oversight bodies (NKÚ, Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže / ÚOHS decisions on procurement challenges) not covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add NKÚ kontrolní závěry and the ÚOHS decision database (sbírky rozhodnutí) as indirect sources; ÚOHS decisions name the disputed tender, the authority and often internal responsibilities.

coverage_gaps.description: The supplier ecosystem revealed by contract awards (acquirers, processors, systems integrators) has no dedicated source yet — only the registers that name them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a supplier watchlist from VVZ/TED winner fields, then track those firms' own career pages and ARES/Obchodní rejstřík statutory-body changes for leadership moves.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only TED was captured in en, and no en-language reporting on Czech state payments procurement.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add en queries against TED, EU Commission country reports and English Czech outlets to catch cross-border supplier announcements not published in cs.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetched; all endpoints are search-derived and unverified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every source_url and example_url, treating 403/timeouts as bot-defence rather than death, and confirm the VVZ domain migration.

coverage_gaps.description: Accenture CZ, PwC CZ and IBM/NCR Atleos CZ were not covered with dedicated local-language sources; PwC in particular was not searched at all in this slice.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run dedicated cs queries per firm ('PwC Česká republika nový partner finanční sektor', 'Accenture Praha bankovnictví posiluje tým') and crawl each firm's CZ newsroom directly rather than relying on search.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side job postings — the most direct A5 signal in this cell — remain uncollected. Careers pages of Trask, Aricoma/Cleverlance, Asseco CE, Monet+, ArnaThora, Loomis CZ and G4S CZ were identified as targets but not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-vendor careers-page crawler plus targeted queries against jobs.cz/prace.cz/StartupJobs employer profiles; track posting counts and role titles (core banking konzultant, EMV, ATM technik, integrace) as a demand index.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech commercial-register sources (ARES / justice.cz / or.justice.cz Sbírka listin) were not exercised, though they give vendor headcount, revenue and statutory-body changes for CZ subsidiaries of every actor in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ARES + Sbírka listin lookups keyed on IČO for each vendor entity; statutory-body changes are a clean, dated leadership-move signal independent of PR.

coverage_gaps.description: ICZ, KB SmartSolutions, Adastra, GEM System, Komix and other mid-tier CZ bank integrators were not reached within this slice's query budget.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from CIO.cz 'Případová studie' hubs and ChannelWorld partner-programme coverage to enumerate the mid-tier integrator layer, then treat each as its own reference+careers source.

coverage_gaps.description: Most located personnel evidence dates to 2025 or earlier; no 2026 vendor FS-leadership appointments were confirmed in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run cs personnel queries constrained to 2026 and subscribe to epravo.cz / cfotrends.cz / ceskenoviny.cz feeds for continuous capture rather than point-in-time search.

coverage_gaps.description: Only Zlatá koruna (/soutez/{YEAR} back to ~2009) and ČNB were confirmed to expose a deep, systematically addressable past-edition archive. For most conference sites in this cell the archive depth was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For every event source, enable self-snapshotting from the first crawl and run a one-off Wayback Machine backfill of /program, /recnici, /prednasejici, /speakers paths so a two-edition baseline exists immediately rather than in twelve months.

coverage_gaps.description: Almost every source found is Prague-centred, with Brno appearing only via FinTech Roadmap's earlier editions. No Ostrava/Brno/Plzeň regional banking or payments event was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted cs queries such as 'konference bankovnictví Brno', 'fintech konference Ostrava', 'regionální finanční konference' and check regional venue and chamber-of-commerce calendars.

coverage_gaps.description: Card schemes, acquirers, PSPs and POS/terminal vendors are only indirectly represented (via Mastercard at Banka roku and Economia's card conference). No dedicated CZ acquiring/merchant-services event was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query cs terms 'akceptace platebních karet konference', 'platební terminály konference', 'akvizice obchodníků', and check the ČBA and Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) event calendars specifically.

coverage_gaps.description: The glossary built during this run covers award/jury and speaker terminology (porota, odborná porota, přednášející, řečníci, panelisté, medailonky diskutujících, ročník, program) but the title-normalisation vocabulary for CZ banking roles was only partially exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an explicit cs->en title mapping (generální ředitel/CEO, člen představenstva/board member, ředitel divize, výkonný ředitel, hlavní ekonom, produktový ředitel, CIO/ředitel IT) before diffing rosters, otherwise cosmetic title translations will register as false promotions.

coverage_gaps.description: University-industry coverage rests almost entirely on VŠE Praha. Other CZ finance faculties (Masarykova univerzita ESF, VŠB-TU Ostrava, Univerzita Karlova IES) were not searched for industry panels or career-day rosters.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query each faculty's aktuality feed in cs for 'panelová diskuse banka', 'kariérní den', 'přednáška z praxe' and add any recurring industry panels to the collection set.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice has been verified for liveness; several were derived from search-result summaries rather than direct fetch. Only zlatakoruna.info and paymentsummit.cz were fetched directly during this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over all example_urls before scheduling, and treat any 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than death.

coverage_gaps.description: No per-bank union organisation website or newsletter was located for the big three (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Komerční banka). ZO entities are confirmed to exist as registered legal persons (multiple IČOs each) and OSPPP has per-employer subpages, but their own communication channels (intranet-only in many cases) were not found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from https://www.osppp.cz/nase-sluzby/odborove-organizace to enumerate every per-employer subpage; search each ZO name plus 'zpravodaj'/'informace pro členy'; check Facebook groups. Consider direct contact with OSPPP for public statements.

coverage_gaps.description: This slice is bank-heavy. Payments-specific employers (payment institutions, card processors, fintechs, shared-service/offshoring centres run by banking groups in Brno/Ostrava) were not separately searched for workforce/union coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run Czech queries on 'centrum sdílených služeb banka Brno propouštění', 'platební instituce zaměstnanci', 'back office banky Ostrava rušení' and check CzechInvest/regional development agency announcements of finance-sector service-centre openings and closures.

coverage_gaps.description: No FOI-style collection path was tested. The Czech Freedom of Information Act (zákon č. 106/1999 Sb.) could compel Úřad práce ČR to disclose mass-redundancy notifications by NACE sector and possibly by employer.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pilot a written 106/1999 request to ÚP ČR for mass-redundancy notifications in CZ-NACE section K over the last 36 months; treat as a recurring quarterly request if fruitful.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin and mostly EU-level (Eurofound ERM, UNI Europa). No Czech-based English-language outlet covering bank labour disputes was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test Expats.cz, Czech Radio International (english.radio.cz) and CTK/ČTK English wire for finance-sector layoff coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: ČNB branch-count data was confirmed to exist and be cited by media, but the exact ARAD time-series identifier for branch / business-place counts was not pinned down in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Navigate the ČNB ARAD database explicitly to locate the series for 'počet poboček' / 'obchodní místa' and record the stable series code and export endpoint.

coverage_gaps.description: Only three kraj-level media markets (MS, Jihomoravský, Královéhradecký) are represented; ten remain unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the full Deník edition list from denik.cz plus one independent outlet per remaining kraj (as Patriot serves MS), and add them as low-priority sweep sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech-language standalone discussion forums (non-Reddit) are entirely absent from the candidate set.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe candidate forum hosts with cs queries such as 'fórum bankovní úředník plat diskuze', 'diskuze zaměstnanci ČSOB', and check comment sections of Měšec.cz/Peníze.cz as a proxy forum layer.

briefs: The CZ regulator layer is unusually well instrumented at the ENTITY level and largely silent at the PERSON level. ČNB concentrates everything in JERRS, exposed three ways — an interactive register, seven open CSV datasets under nařízení vlády 425/2016 Sb., and documented WS JERRS XML web services — making new entrants, licence scope and licence withdrawal cheaply diffable, and this is reinforced by the pravomocná rozhodnutí archive, the annual Zpráva o výkonu dohledu, and ČNB's own press releases and Bank Board page for regulator-side leadership and reorganisation. What was NOT found is any public ČNB list of individuals approved under the souhlas s výkonem funkce / vhodnost a způsobilost regime, nor any disclosure of the 30-day advance notifications of statutory-body changes; the practical A5 route is therefore an IČO-keyed join from ČNB registers to obchodní rejstřík / ARES statutory-body diffs, with EBA's PSD2 central register as an independent cross-check on the payments population. Priority build order: WS JERRS and ČNB open data, then the commercial-register officer diff, then press releases, enforcement decisions and the ČNB vacancy board as corroborating and leading indicators.

Czech bank newsrooms are a strong, primary-source-rich surface for A5: the big four (KB, Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, MONETA) plus Raiffeisenbank all run structured, year- or date-partitioned Czech press archives that name incoming and outgoing board members, their portfolios and exact effective dates, and the listed issuers (KB, MONETA) duplicate the same events in mandatory investor disclosures that are cleaner still. Smaller and newer players (Trinity, Partners Banka, Creditas, Air Bank, Fio) publish real leadership news but on thinner, less regular surfaces — often a single slug page rather than an indexed archive — so their index paths need nav resolution before crawling. Czech payment institutions are the weak flank: Global Payments Česko and Worldline CZ have localised sites but no observable Czech appointment-release stream, pushing that signal to the ČTK Protext wire and to registry sources outside this cell. Recommended posture: weekly crawls of the five large newsrooms plus investor-disclosure pages as the backbone, monthly crawls of the small banks, and Protext/Peníze.cz as pointer feeds that flag when a primary release exists.

The Czech public-sector route to banking/payments org-change intelligence rests on four statutory registers — NEN (nen.nipez.cz), the Věstník veřejných zakázek (now vvz.nipez.cz), Registr smluv (smlouvy.gov.cz, administered by DIA since April 2023) and TED — which together name both the state project owners and the winning supplier ecosystem. Hiring and leadership signals come from a parallel statutory feed, ISoSS (portal.isoss.cz) for civil-service posts, complemented by the career pages of the state-enterprise layer: SPCSS, ČNB, DIA, ČSSZ and Česká pošta. Hlídač státu is the most efficient pointer/aggregator for cross-linking contracts, tenders and subjects via a documented API, with portal.gov.cz and portal-vz.cz as the authoritative map of which register currently lives where. The main weaknesses of this cell are the missing municipal tier, the absent audit layer (NKÚ, ÚOHS), and the fact that no URL here has yet been fetched — every endpoint is search-derived and awaits the deterministic liveness pass.

CZ systemic banks are private, so the supplier layer is the primary observable: Temenos (Komerční banka core migration, with Syncordis and LTIMindtree as named partners) and Diebold Nixdorf (ČSOB case study, KB as DN Series pilot with its COO quoted) are the highest-value vendor-published traces, and domestic integrators — Trask, Aricoma/Cleverlance, Asseco CE, Monet+, ArnaThora — carry the rest. Leadership-move signal in this cell is concentrated in Big Four Czech newsrooms (KPMG's annual partner-promotion release, EY's cs_cz newsroom, Deloitte's leadership roster) with epravo.cz, cfotrends.cz and ceskenoviny.cz acting as fetch-friendly mirrors; Accenture and PwC lack an equivalent CZ-language channel. A notable back-door found this run is smlouvy.gov.cz, where private banks' own cash-handling standard contracts (e.g. KB's universal cash-in-packaging agreement) become public whenever the counterparty is a public body, complementing the Loomis and G4S CZ service pages on the cash-handling side. The main unclosed gap is vendor-side job postings — the most direct A5 hiring signal here — which need per-vendor careers-page crawling plus ARES/Sbírka listin statutory-body tracking rather than search-engine discovery.

The CZ events-and-awards layer is unusually rich for role-census purposes: Zlatá koruna's Finanční akademie publishes a named ~400-person roster with employers every year under a stable /soutez/{YEAR} archive going back to roughly 2009, and Mastercard Banka roku publishes a bio'd expert jury plus a CEO-level conference panel each autumn — together these give a free, self-updating, deeply archived time series of who holds which seat. The conference layer splits cleanly by role class: ČBA's Payments Summit and CGI's Trendy v platebním styku expose the payments-operations and transaction-banking layer, IT ve finančnictví the CIO/CISO layer, FinTech Roadmap the founder/innovation layer, VŠE's Rozvoj a inovace finančních produktů and ČNB's speech archive the board and regulator layer, and Blue Events' Retail Summit the merchant/acceptance side. The main structural weaknesses are archive depth outside Zlatá koruna and ČNB (Payments Summit showed no visible past-edition archive on the page fetched, so self-snapshotting plus a Wayback backfill is required to get a two-edition baseline), a strong Prague bias, and no dedicated CZ acquiring/POS-vendor event. Note that two names in the cell brief — 'Banking Summit' and 'Bankovní inovace' — did not resolve to real standalone CZ event brands and are logged as negative findings rather than invented sources; note also that this cell yields incumbency and title-drift signal but essentially no vacancy or hiring-volume signal, which must come from other cells.

Workforce-level org change in Czech banking is legible through three distinct layers. First, the union layer is unusually concentrated: a single sector union, OSPPP (member of ČMKOS), covers ~150 basic organisations across 27+ banks and insurers, publishes a higher-level collective agreement, and is the actor that reliably makes downsizing visible — its firm-level ZO entities are individually registered in the public registry, giving a clean actor map. Second, the statutory layer (Labour Code mass-redundancy notification to Úřad práce ČR, plus mandatory consultation with the union or works council) generates a paper trail, but ÚP publishes only aggregates and sector groupings, so firm-level detection depends on unions, regional Deník reporting, or a 106/1999 Sb. information request. Third, the statistical layer — ČSÚ NACE-K employment and wages, ISPV occupational earnings, and ČNB branch/business-place counts, with Peníze.cz maintaining a usable per-bank branch-count series and Eurofound ERM logging ≥100-job Czech events — lets contraction be measured even when nobody announces it.

The non-Prague layer for CZ banking jobs/organisation signals rests on three legs: the Deník regional network (one edition per kraj, of which Moravskoslezský, Brněnský and Hradecký are mapped here) plus independent regional outlets such as Magazín PATRIOT and POLAR in Moravia-Silesia; municipal and investment-agency publishers (Ostrava city press releases, Invest in Ostrava's centre directory, ABSL's annual sector report) which quantify shared-service-centre footprints in Brno, Ostrava and Hradec Králové before employers announce anything; and the employee-voice layer, where Atmoskop.cz is clearly the highest-value asset — stable per-employer numeric IDs, review paging and a statistics trend page, with reviews explicitly discussing reorganisation, turnover and layoff fear. Job boards (Jobs.cz sector+kraj filters, cz.indeed.com, Jooble, Práce.cz) are best treated as a counting instrument: regional vacancy volumes per bank are the cleanest early proxy for back-office build-out or contraction, and Eurofound's restructuring database provides a structured cross-check. Main weaknesses this run: no standalone Czech forum was found, Glassdoor is assumed login-walled and scraping-prohibited (unverified), Brno Daily and Ostravan.cz could not be confirmed, and the union / Úřad práce mass-layoff channels — likely the earliest hard signals — remain entirely unmapped.

For CZ banking/payments people intelligence, the reliable English-language layer is not the trade press but the foreign parents themselves: Erste Group, KBC, Société Générale and RBI announce Czech CEO, management-board and country-head changes in English regulated releases, mirrored on GlobeNewswire, Euronext and EQS — these are free, timestamped, and the earliest record. International aggregators (Finextra, The Paypers, FinTech Futures, IBSi, XPRIMM) do cover appointments but showed no systematic Czech coverage in this pass, while bne IntelliNews is the strongest genuine CEE desk and is paywalled; SeeNews and Emerging Europe did not substantiate as CZ people sources. The archive dimension is the cell's distinctive contribution: CZ bank management pages such as rb.cz's Bank Management are stable diff targets, and a Wayback CDX watchlist over 'vedení / představenstvo' pages would catch the org changes companies never announce. Local-language search was run and produced two useful Czech-side anchors (Kurzy.cz corporate wire and oPojištění.cz's dedicated 'Jmenování a odchody' rubric) for cross-dating what the English trackers aggregate.

The CZ payments-employer source landscape splits into three usable layers: company-owned channels (Global Payments CZ, Worldline en-cz, Nexi Central Europe, GoPay's dedicated jobs subdomain, Twisto's 'pro média'), Czech-language trade and business media that actually run appointment columns (fintag.cz 'Personálie', ProfitOnline 'Lidé a společnost', Fintree, FinTech Cowboys, CzechCrunch, Lupa, E15, plus ČTK's Protext wire as the PR backbone), and structural registries (ČNB JERRS/open data for the actor universe, obchodní rejstřík statutory-body changes as the hardest dateable proxy for country-manager churn). LinkedIn is the richest single newsroom for GoPay and Comgate but is login-walled and ToS-restricted, so it must stay a manual-review source. The weakest coverage is the terminal/ATM estate — Euronet, Diebold Nixdorf and NCR/Atos country teams publish essentially nothing in Czech — and card-scheme CZ offices, both of which should be picked up via register monitoring and a dedicated scheme-focused pass. Local-language searching was decisive: the highest-value finds (Protext, fintag Personálie, Twisto and Skip Pay appointment PR) surfaced only on cs queries, not en ones.

Czech people-moves intelligence for banking splits into two layers. The prestige business press — Hospodářské noviny, Týdeník Ekonom, Deník N, and to a lesser degree E15, Euro and Seznam Zprávy — is where unannounced exits, forced departures and restructuring numbers actually break (HN on the ČNB exodus around the Michl governorship; Seznam Zprávy quantifying Komerční banka's ~1,840-post reduction), but three of those are hard-paywalled and none maintains a standing personalia rubric. The de-facto ledgers are elsewhere and mostly open: Bankovnictví online's 'Personálie' column is the sector-precise one, with Newstream's /stitek/personalie and /stitek/kariera tags, Měšec.cz /n/personalie, Peníze.cz's personální-změny topic page, Management News and MediaGuru's annual marketing/PR personnel roll-ups covering the rest. Practical design: use the open ledgers plus Patria's hot-news archive for high-recall event detection, and reserve paid or licensed press-archive access for the paywalled dailies where the reasons behind a departure live. Czech-language collection is non-negotiable here — English-language coverage of these moves is close to nonexistent.

The CZ HR/recruitment intelligence layer for banking splits into three tiers: (1) recurring quantitative instruments — ManpowerGroup's quarterly Index trhu práce with an explicit finance/insurance sector index, plus the annual Hays Mzdový průzkum, Grafton salary survey/Mozaika pracovního trhu, Randstad's salary-benefits and employer-brand studies, and Reed's CZ guide; (2) retained executive search boutiques with Prague offices (Amrop, Boyden, Stanton Chase, Hays Executive) whose practice pages and placement news carry leadership-move signals; and (3) a dense Czech-language pointer layer — hrnews.cz, hrforum.cz (Asociace personalistů/People Management Forum), personalista.com, plus PR wires kurzy.cz, e15.cz and penize.cz — that republishes the gated recruiter reports in open form. No recruiter publishes a banking-only CZ report: sector signal must be reconstructed from sector chapters and index values. Two non-obvious high-value finds sit outside the classic recruiter set: finak.cz's monthly tally of financial-adviser moves between distribution networks, and the sector trade union OSPPP, which surfaces headcount, branch-closure and collective-bargaining pressure at named banks.

CZ vacancy intelligence is unusually concentrated: LMC's Jobs.cz ecosystem is both the dominant board and the white-label host for most large banks' own career sites (kb., csob., rb., moneta., unicreditbank.jobs.cz), so one enumeration pattern yields near-complete official coverage of the incumbents. Around it sit StartupJobs.cz and ATS-hosted fintech boards (Twisto on Recruitee) whose ad text discloses tech stack and compliance posture in detail, Prace.cz for branch-network staffing, and the Úřad práce statutory vacancy register as the only officially-mandated feed. The richest leadership signal — LinkedIn Jobs and Glassdoor reviews — is auth-walled and ToS-restricted, so that half of the cell must be budgeted as manual analyst review rather than automated collection. The core methodological point is that no single ad is evidence: value comes from repeated diffing of listing indices over time, which means snapshotting must begin now to establish a baseline.

The self-reported professional social signal for CZ banking and payments is real and rich but structurally hard to collect: LinkedIn is where Czech bankers announce moves first, in both Czech ('nastupuji do', 'jsem hrdý', 'jmenování ředitelem') and English ('excited to join'), yet only profile pages — not post permalinks — are reachable from a logged-out client, so the announcement text itself resists automated capture. X retains official bank accounts (Air Bank, Raiffeisenbank ČR confirmed) but is login-walled and low-signal for personnel news, and Bluesky shows no meaningful Czech banking community at all. The practical architecture is therefore two-layer: a curated manual watchlist of named executive and specialist LinkedIn profiles for early sight, backed by an automated crawl of Czech personnel-change rubrics — bankovnictvionline.cz/personalie above all, plus MediaGuru, e15, Peníze.cz, ManagementNews and NejBusiness — which mirror the same self-reports within days and are openly accessible. The largest remaining gaps are payments-sector actors (acquirers, PSPs, processors) and the mid-level lateral tier that the cell exists to catch.

The CZ statutory-filing layer is unusually strong for A5: every change of statutory body, prokura, branch or registered office is legally mandated, dated twice (den vzniku funkce vs. zapsáno dne), and available both through the official UI (or.justice.cz, migrating to verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz) and as bulk open data (dataor.justice.cz) plus a documented ARES REST API — so a diff-based org-change monitor can be built without scraping. Two structural changes reshape the landscape: the přeměny amendment moved merger projects and creditor warnings out of Obchodní věstník into the Sbírka listin (making the document collection, not the gazette, the M&A early-warning channel), and the Ministry of Justice closed the public Evidence skutečných majitelů and its open data on 17 December 2025, removing free beneficial-ownership tracing. Commercial aggregators (Kurzy.cz relationship graphs, Peníze.cz, Merk, sledovani-insolvence.cz) and the NGO platform Hlídač státu add value chiefly as pointer and alerting layers — person-to-entity pivots that reveal unknown subsidiaries and SPVs — but every lead they generate must be confirmed against the official register. The cell cannot serve 'jobs'/'hiring' at all: CZ registers record only registrable legal facts, not staff-level recruitment.

The CZ regulated-market disclosure channel for banking A5 signal has a clear two-tier shape: ČNB's Centrální úložiště regulovaných informací (CUri/OAM) is the statutory archive of every MAR inside-information item, AGM convocation and annual report for Czech-listed issuers, while the Prague Stock Exchange functions mainly as a timing tripwire that points onward to issuer IR sites. Only MONETA Money Bank and Komerční banka give genuinely Czech, calendar-driven leadership disclosure — their 'povinně uveřejňované informace' and 'valná hromada' pages carry AGM agendas naming supervisory-board candidates roughly a month before appointment, the cell's rare forward-looking signal. For Česká spořitelna, ČSOB and Raiffeisenbank the CZ entity is unlisted, so coverage depends on the foreign parents' ad-hoc feeds (Erste, KBC, RBI, Société Générale, VIG) plus their EQS/Euronext mirrors, which are English-first and reliably dated. Czech-side collection will be scraping-and-PDF work with no RSS or API found, and the biggest structural gap is that payment institutions and unlisted bank subsidiaries fall entirely outside this cell and must be covered by the commercial register and regulator-registry cells.

The Czech association layer is unusually rich as a people-and-pointer source: ČBA (banks, >99% of the sector), ČLFA (leasing/consumer credit), AKAT (capital markets, 100+ members), Česká fintech asociace/ČEFTAS (50-80+ digital-finance firms), SBK (cards/payments) and ČKMA (crypto) all publish member directories and elected governing bodies staffed by named serving executives, and SP ČR's sectoral-association registry lets you enumerate these bodies exhaustively rather than guessing. Bilateral chambers add an English-language layer — AmCham CZ exposes a Finance Committee, a board of country CEOs and a corporate directory — though ČNOPK and the British Chamber could not be confirmed to publish finance-committee rosters in this pass. The highest-value analytical move is diffing these rosters over time and anchoring every person-level fact in the spolkový rejstřík, which timestamps statutory-body changes independently of what the associations choose to publish. Main friction is technical rather than legal: content is public and collectible, but ČBA's committee pages did not yield content to a static fetch and several sites need headless rendering or on-site link discovery.
